title: Contract Standing and the Standby Rate (Workplace Cafe Management Program)
content:
A paused Workplace Cafe Management Program contract may also carry a day of written notice of termination, and the standing of the contract on the day the standby charge is raised settles the standby rate. Where a day of written notice of termination stands on the contract and the suspended days counted reach half the contract year suspension ceiling printed against the service model, the standby rate is the wind-down standby rate, which is 60 per cent. Where a day of written notice of termination stands on the contract and the suspended days counted fall below half the contract year suspension ceiling printed against the service model, the standby rate is the notice standby rate, which is 48 per cent. Where no day of written notice of termination stands on the contract, the standby rate is the standby percentage printed against the service model.

| Standing of the contract | Suspended days counted | Standby rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A day of written notice of termination stands on the contract | Reach half the contract year suspension ceiling printed against the service model | The wind-down standby rate, 60 per cent |
| A day of written notice of termination stands on the contract | Fall below half the contract year suspension ceiling printed against the service model | The notice standby rate, 48 per cent |
| No day of written notice of termination stands on the contract | Whatever they come to | The standby percentage printed against the service model |

The day of written notice of termination is the day that notice stands recorded on the contract. The contract year suspension ceiling is the figure printed against the service model the contract is held in, and the comparison is made against half that ceiling.

**Both sides of the boundary, on hypothetical figures.** Take a hypothetical contract year suspension ceiling printed against the service model of 40 calendar days, so that half that ceiling is 20 calendar days. With a day of written notice of termination standing and 20 suspended days counted, the suspended days counted reach half that ceiling and the standby rate is the wind-down standby rate of 60 per cent. With that notice standing and 19 suspended days counted, they fall below half that ceiling and the standby rate is the notice standby rate of 48 per cent. With 19 suspended days counted and no day of written notice of termination standing on the contract, the standby rate is the standby percentage printed against the service model.
